name: fast-float (Eisel-Lemire float parsing)
verdict_reason: The 2-8x lead over from_str was measured on Rust 1.49. Rust 1.55 merged a port of this crate's algorithm into std, and on Rust 1.81 and 1.83 fast-float is only 1.02x-1.29x faster on five datasets and 1.32x-1.60x slower than std on large integer-valued floats. The crate is abandoned with two RustSec advisories; fast-float2 is the patched fork for byte-slice and partial parsing.
tier_reason: Public benchmark tool (extras/simple-bench) with CPU, OS and Rust version stated for both the old and new tables.
claimed_speedup: README: faster than from_str by 2-8x; Rust 1.49 tables: canada 21.58 vs 174.43 ns (i7-4771), 25.90 vs 190.06 ns (AMD Rome). Current tables (fast-float2 README): canada 9.77 vs 11.59 ns (i7-14700K, Rust 1.81), 19.17 vs 22.90 ns (EPYC 7763, Rust 1.83); bi 57.52 vs 35.92 ns and 82.37 vs 62.20 ns (std faster) (ratios derived from page data)
workload: Best ns per f64 parse on canada.txt, mesh.txt, uniform [0,1), big integer-valued floats (bi/iidi), %de%d and reciprocals of random u32.
hardware: Intel i7-4771 and AMD Rome (Rust 1.49 tables); Intel i7-14700K and AMD EPYC 7763 (current tables)
os: macOS and Linux (1.49 tables); Ubuntu 24.04 WSL2 and Ubuntu 24.04.1 (current tables)
one_liner: Port of Lemire's fast_float that beat std's float parsing 2-8x on Rust 1.49; std absorbed the algorithm in 1.55 and the gap is now 1.0x-1.3x.
how_it_is_fast: Eisel-Lemire: for up to 19 significant digits it computes the result with one or two 64x64-bit multiplications against a table of powers of five, falling back to a slower exact path only for long inputs. On little-endian systems it has extra handling for numbers with more than eight digits after the decimal point.
use_it_when: Never the original crate; use fast-float2 if you need parse_partial or parsing straight from &[u8]
skip_it_when: Ordinary f64/f32 parsing: str::parse is within about 1.3x since Rust 1.55
Any use of the unpatched fast-float crate: RUSTSEC-2024-0379 (unsound) and RUSTSEC-2025-0003 (segfault on empty input)
caveats: The old and new tables come from different CPUs; the ratios within each table are same-machine
The current tables are in the fork's README, written by the author of std's implementation
tradeoffs: Unmaintained since 2021; unsafe code with known soundness bugs

evidence.quote: In particular, it is faster than Rust standard library's `FromStr::from_str()` by a factor of 2-8x
- CPU: Intel i7-14700K 3.40GHz - OS: Ubuntu 24.04 (WSL2) - Rust: 1.81
- CPU: AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core Processor 3.20GHz - OS: Ubuntu 24.04.1 - Rust: 1.83
